verdict.rationale: Forter documents a dedicated agentic-orders flow. Merchants set orderType to AI_AGENT and send transaction-source metadata when an order comes from a consumer's agent (e.g. ChatGPT or Gemini), which Forter says improves its risk decisions on agentic traffic. However, this relies on merchant-side labeling, and the evidence never shows Forter itself telling malicious bots apart from legitimate agents. missing for 10: evidence of Forter-side detection or verification separating malicious bots from legitimate AI agents, documentation that agent-labeled orders are not blanket-declined, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, the product distinguishes malicious bots from legitimate AI buying agents, so agent-driven purchases aren't blanket-blocked as fraud

citations.quote: When a merchant receives an order from a consumer's agent (e.g. ChatGPT or Gemini), they should call the Forter API with additional data, signaling Forter the transaction source as well as transaction metadata
This additional data improves Forter's risk decisions and provides the merchant better reporting on agentic traffic.
